citation.title: A review of irregular time series data handling with gated recurrent neural networks
citation.authors: P.B. Weerakody, K.W. Wong, G. Wang, W. Ela

topic: Review of gated RNN methods (LSTM/GRU variants) for missing values and irregular sampling, mostly in medical, environmental, traffic and activity data
own_question: Which gated-RNN imputation-focused and prediction-focused techniques handle irregular time series?
actual_method_and_evidence: Narrative literature review. It categorises methods by technique, including missing indicators, time-interval decay (GRU-D), bidirectional/seq2seq imputation, GANs, ODE-RNNs and modified cells. It compiles cross-paper metrics on PhysioNet, MIMIC-III and Beijing PM2.5 and notes that the setups are not consistent. It contains no plasma or fusion content and no new experiments.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Irregular-series methods often encode missingness indicators and elapsed time since the last observation, for example through decay toward a past value or a mean.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a review summary of other works. The cited results come from non-plasma datasets. It is background only and does not justify any implemented method.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. Several reviewed imputation methods are bidirectional and noncausal. No real-time timing is reported.
validation_if_relevant: The review notes that comparisons across papers lack common setups. It reports no validation of its own.
forbidden_inferences: that any gated-RNN method suits CES nowcasting
that cross-paper AUC/MAE rankings are valid comparisons
that the review covers plasma diagnostics or ion temperature
that all prior irregular-series work is noncausal
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most an optional generic citation for using elapsed time since the last report and missingness as features. It is not needed for the fusion framing.
